compatNote: COMPATIBILITY FLOOR the base states and every addition inherits (v5 version spine, V5-PLAN 2.2). Floors plus a single proven point, never a support matrix: rolling latest-only means the gate proves exactly one (dw, apps, swift tag) triple per run, and what it proved is recorded upward in layers/INDEX.json gateProven - written by the Foundry, never by hand. `dw.ring` is the Dynamicweb HOSTING ring the artifact was proven on (release policy: R0 is the current milestone under a 30-day soak, R1 the current milestone, R2 current+1, R3 current+2, R4 current+3; milestones move first-in first-out, one ring step per month). The Foundry compat leg compares it as an ORDER against the ring observed on the host: a host in the pinned ring or a newer one PASSes, a host in an OLDER ring PASSes once that ring carries the proven milestone (layers/INDEX.json gateProven.dw.version) and FAILs otherwise naming the month it arrives, and an unreadable ring falls back to that same version comparison. `dw.min` is the platform floor, kept one release as the derived alias of the proven milestone, `dw.tfm` the single target framework the host must build against, `swift.tag` the dynamicweb/Swift release tag (the 3-digit `swiftVersion` above is the same release without the tag form). `apps[].required: false` is an optional companion app: absent is fine, present below `min` is not. An addition MAY restate `compat` in its own layer.json to raise a floor; it may never lower one. THE SPINE IS THE SOURCE: every value in this block is a COPY of the floors of consumer `layers` in versions/spine.json, which also records each floor's reason ref, the package ids with their aliases and retired predecessors (Dynamicweb.MCP is the retired predecessor of Truvio.Commerce.MCP: a host carrying only Dynamicweb.MCP is below the floor) and the proven `current`; tools/ci/Validate-Distribution.ps1 fails when the two disagree. Change the spine first, then copy. A floor rises only when a consumer depends on the fix, never to the latest release (owner ruling redesign-floors, 2026-09-23): a raise needs a new reason.ref in the spine or CI fails. Versions order as SemVer 2.0 with NuGet prerelease labels, so a floor names the version as the package ships it (0.6.0-beta, not 0.6.0).
minSerializerVersionDeprecated: DEPRECATED ALIAS, not a second floor. The one serializer floor is compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min: the Foundry compat leg (Test-CompatFloors) and the dw-demo-base install step read that key and nothing else. This field repeats the same value for prose readers that still name it (dynamicweb/skills dw-users-permissions page-gating.md); tools/ci/Validate-Distribution.ps1 fails when it disagrees with compat.apps, so it can never state a different number. Raise compat.apps and this field together; remove this field once no reader names it.
serializerTaughtSurfaceNote: WHY THE FLOOR IS 1.0.6-beta (raised 2026-09-22 with sample-data 5.0.1, Distribution #78; it was 1.0.2-beta from base 3.4.2). Layers ship serialized SqlTable rows: sample-data ships its whole demo dataset as merge-mode SqlTable YAML with a per-document ownership header, and feature-rma ships its RMA rows the same way. Four engine facts set the floor. (0) SqlTable tables with NO primary key: 1.0.2-beta and earlier wrote a heap table (DynamicStructures, Languages on DW 10.28) as DELETE FROM plus insert in EVERY mode, so the one Dynamic Workspace row sample-data 5.0.0 merges deleted every workspace the host already had (Foundry #1305, Serializer #21). 1.0.3-beta resolves a match key instead (primary key, then the predicate's declared keyColumns, then a unique index, then all columns), a Merge never deletes, a whole-table truncate happens only under an explicit replaceStrategy truncate, and the run log reports a Deleted count; sample-data declares keyColumns on its DynamicStructures predicate, which an older engine ignores. 1.0.5-beta is the floor rather than 1.0.3-beta because 1.0.3-beta and 1.0.4-beta log a WARNING for every heap entry, declared keyColumns included, and strict mode (the Management API default) fails the whole deserialize on it (Serializer #30, measured by Foundry gate run 20260922-223534); from 1.0.5-beta a declared key is an info line and only inferred keys warn. 1.0.6-beta rather than 1.0.5-beta because 1.0.3-beta to 1.0.5-beta stopped remapping page ids held in option-list fields (Swift's ProductListComponentSelector / ProductComponentSelector ComponentSource and ProductBom ListComponentSource, RadioButtonListEditor with valueField PageId), so a delivered storefront listed zero products (Serializer #32, gate run 20260922-231413); 1.0.6-beta resolves ItemType/Sql option sources with valueField PageId or ParagraphId through the page and paragraph maps whatever the editor. (1) SqlTable NULL round trip: Truvio.Commerce.Serializer 1.0.1-beta and earlier wrote a NULL column as 1900-01-01 / '' / 0 in Merge mode on a row where an empty-string column came before the NULL (Serializer issue #18); 1.0.2-beta is the first release that writes it back as NULL, so an older engine silently corrupts shipped rows. (2) PackageUnzip, the transport an online build uses to move a layer's files, is available from 1.0.1-beta. (3) The ownership header needs 1.0.0-beta or later: a 0.9.x engine fails strict on the unknown ownership column. The engine's taught surface (the skills corpus and the Foundry harness) may run ahead of this floor; the floor rises only when a layer ships something an older engine drops, rejects or corrupts. Raise compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min and minSerializerVersion together, not this note.
description: Machine-readable guarantees the base layer makes to every addition (v3.0 Distribution, base 3.0.0 FRAMEWORK-ONLY). The Swift 2.4 base split moved ALL content (both mode trees) and UrlPath to the surface-swift layer; the base now ships only the framework SQL sets + this contract + SQL-predicate config. Additions (feature/sample-data/surface/theme layers) bind ONLY to this contract - never to each other. Content-scoped contract bits (content areas, langPrefix, navDepth, page anchors, title rules, per-environment Area exclusions, protected Swift item types) moved to layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json. The gate reads this file for the base-contract collision check.

idRules.nvarcharPkNote: When an addition writes rows into a base-owned table whose PK is nvarchar (most Ecom tables - PriceId, PaymentId, ProductId, etc.), it MUST namespace the PK with a PACK-<NAME>- prefix (uppercase layer name). Keeps additions disjoint from the base and from each other.
idRules.intIdentityNote: When an addition writes SqlTable rows keyed by an int-identity PK, it MUST reserve an id at or above the 100000 floor. The floor does not reach _content item-instance ids (ItemType_<systemName> rows written through a page or paragraph): ItemType_* Id is a non-identity nvarchar the platform allocates on insert, and the Serializer content provider re-creates item rows by page/paragraph uniqueId, so the target assigns its own id and a YAML fields.Id never lands as the stored id. fields.Id in _content is informational only; no validator checks an item-id floor on _content. The floor applies to the int ids a layer MINTS. The AccessUser ids this contract names in guaranteedRows.permissionGroups are the one explicit exception: the permission groups 1325 / 1270 / 1292 are base-owned and sit below the floor by contract, and the base ships exactly those ids as SqlTable rows. Every identity the sample-data layer mints is above the floor (the B2B account 100100 and the personas 100101 / 100102 / 100103). Any other id below 100000 is out of contract. No validator checks the int-identity floor; it is an authoring rule.
idRules.baseCatalogNote: The base ships ZERO catalog (scaffolding-only, swift/2.3.2): EcomGroups, EcomProducts, EcomGroupProductRelation, EcomVariantGroups, EcomVariantsOptions, EcomVariantOptionsProductRelation, EcomDiscount, EcomDiscountTranslation, EcomPrices carry no base rows. The collision surface for these tables is addition-vs-sample-data-vs-addition, arbitrated statically by the gate.
idRules.reservedFixtureNote: The sample-data layer's demo catalogue, personas and orders reserve these key prefixes (the TC* family, mirrored in that layer's costHints.reservedKeyPrefixes). Additions must not use them. An addition writing rows of its own into a base-owned table uses its own PACK-<NAME>- prefix instead (nvarcharPkPrefix).
idRules.noPerItemTypeNumericTableNote: The contract is prefix-based, not per-itemType-numeric. There is deliberately NO per-itemType numeric range table - do not invent one.

guaranteedRows.permissionGroupsNote: DW 10.26.9 has no AccessUserGroup table - groups ARE AccessUser rows of type 2.
guaranteedRows.usersNote: users and memberships are NOT base rows. They ship in the sample-data layer as merge-mode SqlTable YAML (merge/_sql/AccessUser, merge/_sql/AccessUserGroupRelation) and every entry carries presentOnlyWhen: sampleData - they exist only when an edition activates sampleData: true. An edition with sampleData: false has no AccessUser 100101 / 100102 / 100103 and no memberships, so a sign-in, persona or customer-number binding against them finds no row. All three personas belong to the one B2B account (AccessUser 100100, customer number TC-100200) and carry that same customer number, because contract prices, account-wide favourites and the CSR account listing compare the string exactly. No password is in the data: the sample-data predicate excludes AccessUserPassword and the credential is set online through the Management API UserSetPassword command. A layer probe that needs a persona names it in its requiresFixtures. Only permissionGroups are base-owned (baseOwnedTables.replaceFiltered FILTER-01).

referenceCategory.note: Hidden template category (CategoryType 2) that Dynamicweb's completeness-rule and category-field admin UI reads; required by DemoVerifier Check 2. SHIPPED BY THE BASE since 3.6.0 as two filtered Replace predicates (baseOwnedTables.replaceFiltered FILTER-02 / FILTER-03). Before 3.6.0 the row was claimed here but never shipped: only the Foundry gate synthesised it pre-host-start (Invoke-SeedVerify.ps1 Step 3b), so a consumer deserializing the Distribution outside the gate never received it (Foundry #1304). The gate seed stays and is IF NOT EXISTS-guarded on the category id, so a host it already seeded with a LANG1 translation keeps that row; the base ships the ENU translation, matching every other ENU-keyed display name in the Distribution. Seeded pre-host-start matters because DW caches categories at startup.

contractPrice.note: Ships in the sample-data layer next to the product it scopes to (merge/_sql/EcomPrices/TC-PRICE-CTR-0046.yml); present only when an edition activates sampleData: true. It is the subject of feature-pricing's cart-price contract probe: signed in as the buyer the cart charges 36.90 against a 45.00 list and a 39.60 customer-group row, with zero custom code.

sampleData.note: What the ONE sample-data layer guarantees to an addition that binds to it. Since sample-data 4.0.0 there is exactly one layer of kind sample-data and it carries the whole demo dataset: the browsable Truvio Commerce catalogue, the three personas on one B2B account, the buyer's orders, quotes, carts and favourite lists, the storefront copy, the demo clock and the email-marketing statistics backfill. Since 5.0.0 it also carries the PIM STRUCTURE those category fields always needed - a ShopType 4 shop, a data-model folder, four data models, four completion rules with their reference_category mirrors, and one Dynamic Workspace - named below. An addition NEVER binds to the layer directly - it binds to the subjects named here and declares them in its behaviorProbes requiresFixtures. Every subject is absent when an edition sets sampleData false, and a probe that names one is then recorded as a loud SKIP, never a silent pass.

buyer.note: surface-swift's authenticated my-returns probe signs in as this persona, and so does every cart-price and checkout-recurring probe. The customer-center dashboard data (customerCenter below) belongs to this persona.

csr.note: The CSR customer-center surfaces surface-swift ships resolve against this persona; no probe addresses it by id.

accountAdmin.note: The account surfaces under Customer center/Account resolve against this persona; no probe addresses it by id.

skuValidationProduct.note: feature-reordering's sku-validation probe types this ProductNumber into the Quick Order pad's validation feed.

quantityTierProduct.note: feature-pricing's cart-price tier probe adds quantity 10 and expects 96. Quantity 10 is the only rung the customer-group row TC-PRICE-GRP-0020 (108 at quantity 1, group 1325) cannot also produce, so the observed amount proves the tier ladder rather than price resolution in general.

contractPriceProduct.note: feature-pricing's cart-price contract probe adds quantity 1 signed in as the buyer and expects 36.90.

bomKitProduct.note: feature-bom-configurator's bom-cart-lines probe posts the two slot ids with a NON-default child in each (TCPROD0003, TCPROD0052) and expects two child lines. TCPROD0041 is the fixed Bundle Kit and carries no EcomProductItems slot, so the configurable kit TCPROD0042 is the subject.

subscriptionProduct.note: feature-subscription-orders' checkout-recurring probe buys this plan on PAY2 / SHIP9 and asserts a new EcomRecurringOrder row for the buyer.

deliveredOrder.note: surface-swift's authenticated my-returns probe (moved there from the retired feature-rma layer) returns against this completed order; its first line is what the RMA link points at.

rma.note: A sample-data row since sample-data 6.0.0: the retired feature-rma layer shipped EcomRmas PACK-RMA-0001 and its EcomRmaOrderLines link (id 100301, above the intIdentityFloor), and both moved into sample-data with their keys unchanged, beside the deliveredOrder subject they bind to. The PACK- prefix predates the move and stays, because a re-key would leave the old row on every delivered host. The my-returns probe that reads it is declared by surface-swift, the layer that ships the My returns page, with requiresFixtures TCO-0001.

customerCenter.note: The data the surface-swift customer-center dashboard (Swift 2.4 Dashboard widgets, surface-swift 1.16.0) draws for the buyer persona, added in sample-data 6.0.0. Every order is USD because the Spent this month and Monthly spending widgets sum one currency only and print '-' when the result mixes currencies; the Swift area and every EcomPrices row are USD too, so an order the demo places joins the same sum. The order widgets filter on OrderCompletedDate, so completed orders carry one and span the six-month chart window; open orders (OS1) carry none and list only on My orders. Quotes sit in the base quoteStates, three of them in QuotePending, the state the Pending quotes widget asks for. Dates are absolute at the harvest day and the demo clock shifts them daily, so the relative ages hold; the current-month total depends on the day of the month the demo runs.

pimShop.note: The ShopType 4 DataStructure shop that owns the data-model tree, added in sample-data 5.0.0. It is NOT customer-facing and carries no storefront group: the browsable catalogue stays on the base's SHOP1. The index field name is DERIVED FROM THE SHOP NAME (DATAMODEL_<name with spaces as underscores>), which is what the workspace level below and the surface-swift Products.index SkipDataModels=False build both read, so renaming the shop moves that field. No probe addresses it; an addition that wants to add its own data model binds here for the shop id.

dataModelFolder.note: The one GroupType 1 DataModelFolder, the root of the PIM tree. A folder holds no products and carries no ProductCategoryId. It carries its own EcomShopGroupRelation row like every other group: DW resolves a group to its shop through that table and does not walk the parent chain.

dataModels.note: The four GroupType 2 data models, one per product category, added in sample-data 5.0.0. Every DataModel group needs a ProductCategoryId or its fields reach no product. All 61 masters carry an EcomGroupProductRelation row to the data model of their band with IsPrimary FALSE - the master's primary home stays its catalogue subgroup, so the storefront is unchanged. The four categoryId values are the same four the tc_specs display group spans (surface-swift surface.contract-notes.json scopeNote), which is what makes the PDP spec table and the completeness score read one set of fields.

completenessRules.note: One rule per data model, each naming its category's seven fields. The field names are the AUTHORING system name (the pipe form); the INDEX name for the same field is CustomField_<systemName>, and a rule carrying the index form matches nothing. The 28 reference_category MIRROR field rows (+ 28 ENU translations) sample-data ships are what makes the admin completeness panel render at all - the PARENT reference_category row and its translation are base-owned (base 3.6.0). Scoring additionally needs the Completeness feature flag and an index build with SkipCompletionRules False; neither is a layer row, and the layer does not claim them.

workspace.title: Truvio PIM - by data model
workspace.requires: surface-swift Products.index Full build with SkipDataModels False
workspace.note: The one Dynamic Workspace sample-data 5.0.0 ships, with its backing query file. A workspace is a PROJECTION, not storage: it moves no product row. Both level sources are non-analysed keyword fields - an analysed free-text source enumerates lower-cased Lucene term fragments and a numeric source enumerates nodes that open onto zero rows, and neither errors, so a level is checked by the SUM of its node counts against the backing query's own total. Without SkipDataModels False the DATAMODEL_ field is never emitted and level 100171 renders empty nodes.

sampleData.countsNote: EcomProducts 97 = 60 masters + 36 variant rows + the subscription plan TCPROD0061, unchanged by 5.0.0: the PIM tree adds relations, never products. EcomGroups 21 = the 16 browsable storefront groups (4 top + 12 sub, on SHOP1) PLUS the 5 PIM groups on TCSHOP-PIM (1 GroupType 1 folder + 4 GroupType 2 data models). It was 16 before sample-data 5.0.0. The two trees live in different shops and only the storefront 16 are browsable, so an edition that pins 16 is pinning a pre-5.0.0 layer. An edition that activates sampleData pins these in expectedCounts; a composition that does not activate it carries zero catalogue.

anchors.note: The buyer and CSR anchors name the sample-data rows in guaranteedRows.users: present only when an edition activates sampleData: true. Buyer and CSR share one customer number because they are two contacts on one B2B account. Content anchors (area 3, langPrefix /swift-2) moved to surface-swift (base 3.0.0 ships zero content areas).

repositories.name: ProductsFrontend
repositories.note: ProductsFrontend is the storefront search repository the Swift design package ships (Files/System/Repositories/ProductsFrontend/ at the Swift 2.4.0 tag, alongside ProductsBackend). No layer in this Distribution ships it: it arrives with the host's Swift Files overlay, which is why provisionedByGate is false. Every eCom_ProductCatalog surface this Distribution ships binds it by path - surface-swift Shop PLP (IndexQuery + FacetGroups), surface-swift desktop header search, surface-swift Express Buy, surface-dap-portal Product Assets and Search results, feature-bom-configurator Kit Configurator. A storefront PLP that cannot list products answers HTTP 200 in both of its failure shapes, never a 500. (1) Repository present over an index of zero documents: the page carries an in-page dw-error block with the Lucene 'numHits must be > 0' ArgumentException. (2) Repository absent: the catalog app renders an EMPTY swift-v2_app div with no product list, no facet rail and no error text of any kind, so the page passes a status scan AND an error-text scan while showing nothing. Gate the PLP on a positive subject (at least one product-card element) plus dw-error == 0, never on HTTP status or on the absence of error text alone.

currencyRates.note: EcomCurrencies.CurrencyRate is hundredths against the default currency. Since base 4.0.0 the default is USD at 100, flagged CurrencyIsDefault true on every USD$$<lang> row: DW resolves the default currency per language context, and a single global default aborted the Products index at 0 documents (base 3.1.2). EUR ships at 100 as well, one-to-one parity with the default, a deliberate demo value and not an exchange rate, so a composition whose prices are EUR renders them unchanged. A non-default currency at rate 1 renders every price in it a hundred times over, with correct symbol and culture formatting, no error and no log entry (measured on DW 10.28.10: a stored 45.00 served as $4,500.00 at USD rate 1). No shipped row carries a rate at or below 1. The default flag is NOT what a storefront serves: the area binding (AreaEcomCurrencyId) decides the currency of a cart and which EcomPrices.PriceCurrency rows match, and an UNBOUND area on DW 10.28 resolves the request culture's currency (Foundry #1232, measured on foundry-sd4v.mydwsite4.com: cart CART783 OrderCurrencyCode USD, TCPROD0046 served 45.00 instead of the contract price 36.90). The area binding belongs to the surface layer that ships the area: surface-swift binds the Swift 2 area to USD from 1.16.0, and every EcomPrices and EcomOrders row the sample-data layer ships is USD from 6.0.0, so binding and prices move together. The other non-default rows carry the values of the source solution and are not maintained exchange rates; a solution that needs real conversion sets real rates, keeping the default at 100 and every other rate relative to it.

quoteStates.note: The quote lifecycle the Swift 2.4 customer-center dashboard reads. Swift's Pending quotes widget (Swift-v2_Dashboard_List/QuotesPending.cshtml) asks /dwapi/ecommerce/orders/search for Type=quote and StateId=QuotePending, so a state with that EXACT id must exist or the widget renders its empty state forever. The ids are the literal Swift ids, not prefixed: the base owns the table and the template hard-codes the id. QuotePending is the flow default, so a quote a customer submits lands in it; the stock OS8 'New' quote state is no longer the default and OS8 / OS9 'Price given' stay in the flow (sort 5 and 6) because a Replace predicate never deletes a row and an older host keeps them either way. No EcomOrderStateRules row is added: the two stock rules (OS8 <-> OS9) stay, and the four states carry no rule, which leaves every transition open, the shape the marine demo ran its quote lifecycle on. OrderStateAutoId is an identity column outside the key, so the host allocates it; the serialized value is informational. Quote orders of the sample-data layer bind here (OrderIsQuote true, OrderStateId one of these four).

country.note: The base has no default-country column: a storefront's default country is its area's AreaEcomCountryCode, owned by the surface layer that ships the area, and EcomCountries.US$$ carries CountryCurrencyCode USD. The base makes US the default for the country-scoped method relations below.

marketDefaults.note: The neutral market default an edition gets with no market work: USD, on-account invoicing with Net 30 terms, four generic delivery methods and Tax labels. Every PaymentId, ShippingId and VatGroupId is kept and only renamed, reconfigured or deactivated, for two reasons. (1) A Replace predicate is an upsert by key and never deletes a row absent from the tree, so a dropped Danish carrier would stay ACTIVE on every host delivered from base 3.x; shipped inactive, it is switched off there too. (2) Other layers post the ids: feature-subscription-orders' checkout-recurring probe buys on PAY2 / SHIP9, which is why those two are the on-account payment and the standard ground method. PaymentAddInType None is the gateway-less checkout handler, which also implements IRecurring. Credit card is inactive because it has no gateway: active, it placed orders unpaid. The Danish language rows (DAN) of the same ids carry Danish translations of the neutral names. A demo for another market rewrites these rows the other way in a demo-local layer.

replaceFiltered.note: FILTER-01: only the three permission groups are base-owned on AccessUser; the sample-data account and personas (100100-100103) ship in that layer as merge rows, never serialized into the base.

FILTER-02: only the hidden reference_category template row (CategoryType 2) is base-owned on EcomProductCategory. The concrete tc_* product categories are sample-data merge rows, so this predicate is filtered and never whole-table - a whole-table Replace here would wipe the layer's categories on every re-deserialize (Foundry #1304).
FILTER-03: the ENU display name 'Reference category' that belongs to the FILTER-02 row, on the same filtered reasoning. The tc_*$$ENU translations stay sample-data-owned (Foundry #1304).

baseOwnedTables.note: Additions touching a base-owned table follow idRules (prefix / floor) and must pass the static intersection checks below. Base ships zero catalog (see idRules.baseCatalog) and zero content areas (base split 3.0.0). UrlPath is surface-swift-owned (its single row is a friendly-URL redirect bound to area 3 + a Swift page id - no route targets exist in a framework-only base).

stockLocations.note: Neutral, brand-free stock locations shipped as TWO whole-table Replace sets - EcomStockLocation and its EcomStockLocationTranslations rows, which is where the name Dynamicweb actually renders lives. Both carry the same three ids on ENU. The baseline DB carried the Swift demo's own 'BikeShop Copenhagen' / 'BikeShop Aarhus' rows, so every composed edition delivered a bike shop's warehouse names; 3.6.0 corrects the names in the base instead of per-edition (Foundry #1303). The IDS 1-3 ARE DELIBERATELY KEPT: all 61 EcomStockUnit rows in the sample-data layer carry StockUnitStockLocationId 3, and EcomShops.ShopStockLocationID (SHOP1 ships 0, meaning 'no single location') addresses the same id space, so a rekey above the intIdentityFloor would orphan the stock units and silently change what a shop points at. These three ids are therefore the one further documented exception to idRules.intIdentityFloor, alongside the permission groups: they are base-owned rows the base does not mint but adopts from the platform baseline. An addition that needs its own stock location mints one at or above 100000. StockLocationCategoryId stays as the baseline carries it (1 and 3 STOCKLOCCAT1 'Click and collect', 2 STOCKLOCCAT2 'Warehouse'): EcomStockLocationCategory is BASELINE-OWNED, serialized by no layer, and the base's Customer pickup delivery method (SHIP5, the StockLocationShippingProvider on STOCKLOCCAT1, named Click & Collect before 4.0.0) needs pickup locations in that category.

collisionChecks.rule: Intersect an addition's _sql/<Table>/*.yml filenames (= row keys; composite keys join with $$) with the base's filenames for the same table. Non-empty = FAIL.
WR-10: the same table+filename shipped by >1 active addition = FAIL. A single layer shipping the same key in its own replace+merge is NOT a collision.

07-01: an addition's fragment-shipped _content relative paths must be disjoint from base _content paths (union of both mode trees); cross-layer parity; shipped-files-only (referenced base anchors excluded); declared-footprint parity (every Content entry matches a declared fragmentContent {areaId, path}).

WR-04: (itemType, fields.Id) pairs land as PK rows in shared ItemType_<systemName> tables. The same pair by >1 owner = FAIL. Reusing an id NUMBER across DIFFERENT itemType tables is fine (PK surface is per-table).

registrationAsymmetry.rule: Every csLedger entry with registration 'addin-attribute-config-row' MUST have >=1 matching configRows entry.
registrationAsymmetry.note: Cross-field rule enforced at activation (not JSON-Schema-expressible); locked by tests.

movedToSurfaceSwift.note: Moved by the base split (Swift 2.4 roll-forward): perEnvironmentAreaExclusions, protectedItemTypes, content anchors (areas/langPrefix), navDepth obligation, title-integrity rules. See layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json.
